title: Nine Hairs of Sable
subtitle: 绘画艺术 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 绘画艺术（文学艺术与体育·绘画、建筑等领域的代表作品和人物）
meta: 主题语境：绘画艺术（文学艺术与体育·绘画、建筑等领域的代表作品和人物）　|　核心词汇：brush　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 brush 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1950 my mother was sent to wash ① a brush she could not hold, and she said the holding was the whole of the lesson. The ② brush, meaning the tool and not the stroke, was nine hairs wide and was cleaned by whoever came last; a brush, she said, is the only thing in a jar that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ brush in that jar had the same handle, and the ④ brush at the front, meaning the one the painter kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever washed properly. A brush, my grandmother said, is nine parts sable and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the sable is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ brush was the whole of the painting, meaning the stroke it made and not the tool. The ⑥ brush, meaning the stroke and not any of that, is the only thing in a studio that everybody borrows and nobody questions; a brush, he said, is either something you wash or the only word that means both a tool and a stroke. She said the stroke is the part they remember.

By 1966 the ⑦ brush had become a photograph in a report, and the report had become an argument about the sable. The ⑧ brush of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine hairs and eleven years of washing; a brush, she said, is either the one at the front or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ brush I remember is the one at the front, which was worn down in 1971 and is still described as the best in the county. A ⑩ brush, my grandmother said in 1974, is the only thing that improves by being worn; every brush, she said, is a stroke that has agreed to look like a tool. She said the stroke was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 画笔（指那支笔本身，与笔触相对）
C. 固定搭配：wash a brush 洗一支画笔
D. n. 画笔（指笔筒里每一支）
E. n. 画笔（指前面那一支）
F. n. 笔触；画法（抽象：与那支笔相对）
G. n. 那幅画、那道笔触（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a brush she could not hold
The brush, meaning the tool and not the stroke
brush was the whole of the painting
the brush had become a photograph in a report
The brush of the whole thing
A brush, my grandmother said in 1974

answers.why: wash a brush 意为“洗一支画笔”，1950 年母亲被派去洗一支她握不住的画笔。
brush 意为“画笔”，指那支笔本身而不是笔触，宽九根毛，由最后走的人洗干净。
brush 指笔筒里每一支画笔，每一支都是同样的笔杆。
brush 指前面那一支（画家留的那一支），是唯一有人认真洗过的。
brush 意为“笔触、画法”，与那支笔相对，父亲说 brush 就是那幅画的全部。
brush 为抽象用法，指那道笔触本身，是画室里人人都借、却没人质疑的东西。
brush 意为“画笔、刷子”，到 1966 年这支 brush 成了报告里的一张照片。
brush 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九根毛和十一年的清洗。
brush 意为“画笔”，我记得的是前面那一支，1971 年被用秃，至今仍被说成全县最好的。
brush 为抽象总称，祖母说画笔是唯一会因为被用旧而变好的东西。
